items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: In that place I had Lee Collins on trumpet. John Marrero on guitar. No, he was playing banjo. His brother on bass. Joe Robichaud on piano.

ctx.x: Well they didn't have anything particular. I just liked a lot of ragtime stuff, jump stuff. I didn't like nothing too slow. Bless me was the blues. Now if you could play the blues for them all night they didn't like that. Just nothing but the blues but nothing slow like stardust or something like that. They didn't like nothing like that. That was too slow they didn't want that. But if you play the blues in that temple right down the alley they liked that. They used to uh get off from work around. And they did a…
Is that Simon or Eddie Marrero on which one? Simon. Simon was on bass.

And drums? Drummer was Alfred William. And yourself, what were you playing then? I was playing clarinet. Still? No, I was playing saxophone then. Yeah, because I started fooling with saxophone when I was at the hummingbird.
